subject: Possible SAE - Subject BR-042-0089 (infusion reaction / ED visit)
body:
Hi Michael,

I need to alert you to a potential SAE for Subject BR-042-0089 (Site 042). The subject received their trastuzumab infusion today (Cycle 4 Day 1) at ~09:10. Approximately 10 minutes after the end of the infusion the patient became lightheaded and had a transient syncopal episode while ambulating in the clinic hallway. Vitals in clinic at the time: BP 82/48 mmHg, HR 110 bpm, SpO2 97% on room air, temperature 36.8°C.

We transported the patient to the ED for evaluation. ED notes (attached) indicate the patient received IV fluids and one dose of diphenhydramine 50 mg IV. Cardiac enzymes were drawn (troponin I 0.01 ng/mL), ECG without acute ischemia. No admission — discharged home the same day at 14:30 after observation. There was no documented change in LVEF in the ED (baseline LVEF 62% from echo dated 2024-11-01 in chart).

We began the SAE form but it's incomplete — missing CTCAE grade, causality/relatedness assessment, and concomitant meds list. We're unsure if this meets SAE criteria per Protocol v3.2 Section 8.3 (expedited reporting) given ED visit/observation. Please advise ASAP whether you need an expedited report to PV/medical monitor and whether we should hold further trastuzumab doses pending sponsor instruction. We have attached the partially completed SAE_Report_Form.pdf and the ED discharge summary.

Thanks,

Emily Clark, BSN, RN
Clinical Research Coordinator
Weill Cornell Medicine - Breast Oncology
Phone: (212) 555-0147
Email: [emily.clark@med.cornell.edu](mailto:emily.clark@med.cornell.edu)

Confidentiality Notice: This message may contain confidential patient information intended only for the named recipient.

subject: Re: Possible SAE - Subject BR-042-0089 (infusion reaction / ED visit)
body:
Hi Emily —

Thanks for the prompt notice and for the attachments. A few quick clarifying points I need to escalate to PV/medical monitor:

1) Was the ED visit documented as an admission or observation stay (i.e., did the patient have an inpatient admission code)? From your note it sounds like same-day discharge — please confirm exact disposition code. 
2) Please provide CTCAE grade for syncope/hypotension or, if not graded yet, your best clinical estimate (Grade 1-4) and whether there was any ongoing medical intervention after discharge.
3) Please confirm the subject's concomitant medications at time of event (especially any new anti-hypertensives, benzodiazepines, or opioid analgesics). 
4) Did the site record this as an SAE in the EDC yet? If yes, provide the eCRF ID; if not, do not delay — we may need an expedited notification depending on PV guidance.
5) Is the subject on any active cardiac meds or any recent change in meds within last 7 days?

Per Protocol v3.2 Section 8.3 we need to review whether this meets criteria for expedited reporting (seriousness = required if led to hospitalization or life-threatening). Even though discharged same day, ED visit for syncope may still meet SAE criteria depending on clinical judgment. I've CC'd PV triage — I will wait for their immediate input but please answer the above items so I can expedite the assessment.

Also, please keep the subject's next trastuzumab dose on hold until we confirm with PV/medical monitor. Document hold in source and note reason as 'safety assessment after infusion reaction.'

Appreciate the quick turn-around on the missing items — I will escalate as soon as I have answers.

Regards,

Michael Reynolds
Clinical Research Associate
Genentech, Inc.
Phone: +1-650-555-2210
Email: [michael.reynolds@gene.com](mailto:michael.reynolds@gene.com)

subject: Re: Possible SAE - Subject BR-042-0089 (infusion reaction / ED visit)
body:
Hi Michael —

Answers below based on chart/ED call-back and medication reconciliation performed by pharmacy:

1) Disposition: ED observation only; patient was not admitted. Discharge time 14:30 same day. (ED record attached shows 'Observation — Discharged to Home')
2) CTCAE grading: We have not formally graded yet — our clinical note lists 'syncope with hypotension, transient.' If I must assign now, our clinic physician documents this as CTCAE Grade 3 for hypotension (medical intervention required — IV fluids). Please advise if you disagree.
3) Concomitant meds: Current meds per MAR: lisinopril 5 mg qd (stable >6 months), acetaminophen PRN, no benzodiazepines or opioids. No new meds in last 14 days. (Pharmacy recon attached)
4) EDC: We have NOT submitted an SAE in EDC yet — we waited for sponsor direction after your previous email. 
5) Cardiac meds/changes: No recent changes. Baseline echo 2024-11-01 LVEF 62% documented in source (attached). No troponin elevation (I=0.01). No chest pain reported.

Attachments: ED_Discharge_Summary_BR-042-0089.pdf (same as earlier), Pharmacy_MedRecon_BR-042-0089.pdf

Per PI on site (Dr. Martin) we have held the next trastuzumab dose in local chart and scheduled telephone follow-up for tomorrow. PI asks sponsor/PV for guidance on expedited reporting and whether an outpatient observation ED visit without admission should be considered an SAE in this context.

Emily

subject: Re: Possible SAE - Subject BR-042-0089 (infusion reaction / ED visit)
body:
Hi Michael —

I reviewed the ED summary and spoke with Emily. Clinically, this appears most consistent with an infusion-related hypotensive reaction to trastuzumab (timing immediate post-infusion and responded to IV fluids). Given the subject required medical intervention (IV fluids and ED observation) I would consider this event serious from a clinical management perspective. 

My provisional plan (pending sponsor/PV guidance):

• Keep trastuzumab doses on hold.
• Repeat vitals and symptom assessment in 24 hours via phone.
• Repeat LVEF in 2 weeks to capture any delayed cardiac effects (baseline 62% as noted). If LVEF falls ≥10% or below 50% we will notify immediately per protocol. 

Please advise if you want the site to submit an expedited SAE now or wait for PV's determination. From the PI perspective, we have documented hold and haven't re-dosed.

Thanks,

Sandra Martin, MD
Principal Investigator
NewYork Cancer Center
Phone: (646) 555-3220
Email: [sandra.martin@nycancercenter.org](mailto:sandra.martin@nycancercenter.org)

subject: Re: Possible SAE - Subject BR-042-0089 (infusion reaction / ED visit)
body:
Michael —

Following Dr. Martin's note we have formally placed the subject's next trastuzumab dose on hold in the chart and flagged the subject as 'pending sponsor instruction.' We have also started a local source note and will schedule an outpatient echo in approximately 2 weeks (requested appt 2024-12-03 pending your confirmation).

Could you please confirm the following as soon as possible:

1) Should we complete and submit the SAE eCRF in EDC now and mark as 'expedited' or wait for PV triage recommendation? (ED visit with observation but no admission.)
2) Is the proposed plan to repeat LVEF in 2 weeks acceptable to sponsor, or do you require a sooner echo and/or cardiology consult? Per protocol v3.2 Section 6.4.2, any symptomatic event may warrant additional cardiac follow-up.
3) Any specific details PV needs entered in the SAE form for causality/relatedness (site tends to prefer sponsor wording when possible).

We need your instruction to proceed — the subject and PI are awaiting guidance and we have documented hold, but we cannot proceed with re-dosing without sponsor direction. Please escalate to the medical monitor/PV if you deem appropriate and advise next steps.

Best regards,

Emily Clark, BSN, RN
Clinical Research Coordinator
Weill Cornell Medicine - Breast Oncology
Phone: (212) 555-0147
Email: [emily.clark@med.cornell.edu](mailto:emily.clark@med.cornell.edu)
